description.narrative:
Ambassaden har beslutat att tillhandahålla icke-öronmärkt stöd till UN Women:s landkontor i Liberia (UNW-LBR) i genomförandet av deras Strategic Note för 2020-2024. Detta utgör ambassadens tredje stöd i ordningen till UNW-LBR.
Den strategiska planen är utformad i linje med UNW:s strategiska plan för 2018-2021, FN:s ramverk för hållbart utvecklingssamarbete i Liberia för 2020-2024 (UNSDCF) samt den nationella utvecklingsstrategin (PAPD 2018-2023). De prioriterade områdena som identifierades i den tidigare strategiska planen bibehålls. Dessa innefattar: stoppa våld mot kvinnor och flickor; kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt; fred, säkerhet och humanitärt bistånd, kvinnors politiska egenmakt och ledarskap.
Utifrån UNW:s globala strategiska plan har ytterligare tre resultatområden identifierats med syfte att öka den organisatoriska effektiviteten, i): stärkt samordning, koherens och ansvarsutkrävande inom FN-systemets åtaganden för jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt, ii) ökat engagemang bland partners för stöd till UNW:s mandat, samt: iii) hög kvalité på programmen genom kunskap, innovation, resultatbaserad styrning (RBM) och utvärdering.
Den strategiska planen för 2020-2024 har bedömts i helhet, finansieringsbeslutet avser dock endast det första inledande året av programmet. Ambassaden utreder för närvarande möjligheten att stödja samarbetspartners inom FN genom att bidra till en FN-gemensam fond, vilken skulle stödja FN:s ramverk för hållbart utvecklingssamarbete i Liberia. Ambassaden har för avsikt att under 2020/2021 se över finansieringsbeslutet på nytt, med möjlighet till fortsatt direktstöd.

The Embassy has agreed to provide non-earmarked support to UN Women Liberia’s (UNW-LBR ) Strategic Note 2020-2024 (Strategic Note). This will be the third support to UNW-LBR.
The Strategic Note is aligned with the UNW Strategic Plan (SP) (2018-2021), Liberia UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2020-2024, and to Liberia’s national development strategy (PAPD 2018-2023). It will retain the same four priority areas identified in the previous Strategic Note. These are: Eliminating Violence Against Women and Girls; Women’s Economic Empowerment; Peace, Security and Humanitarian Assistance; and Governance, Women’s Political Empowerment and Leadership.
There are also three internal results areas focused on increasing organizational effectiveness derived from the global strategic plan i): Enhanced coordination, coherence and accountability of the UN system for commitments to gender equality and women’s empowerment, ii) Increased engagement of partners in support of UNW’s mandate, and: iii) High quality of programmes through knowledge, innovation, results-based management (RBM) and evaluation.
While the whole Strategic Note 2020-2024 will be appraised, the funding decision will cover the 1st year of the programme. The Embassy is currently assessing the possibility of supporting its UN partner agencies by contributing to a UN-developed thematic trust fund that would support the joint UN Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework. The Embassy intends to revisit the funding agreement during 2020/2021, with the possibility of continued direct support.

The Strategic Note is aligned with UN Women's Global Strategic Plan and will contribute to the implementation of the Liberian United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2020-2024). It retains the strategic focus of the previous period and has five outcomes: Outcome 1: By 2024, the most vulnerable and excluded groups have improved quality of life with rights-based, gender sensitive, inclusive, equitable access and utilization of essential social services in an environment free of discrimination and violence including in humanitarian situations. Outcome 2: By 2024, Liberia has sustained, diversified and inclusive economic growth driven by investments in agriculture, food security and job creation and is resilient to climate change and natural disasters. Outcome 3: By 2024, women, girls, men and boys in Liberia experience more sustained peace, inclusive and sustainable growth and development through strengthened formal and informal institutions providing access to effective and equitable justice and security services; promoting and protecting human rights; and strengthening social cohesion and reconciliation. Outcome 4: By 2024, people in Liberia especially the vulnerable and disadvantaged, benefit from strengthened institutions that are more effective, accountable, transparent, inclusive and gender responsive in the delivery of essential services at the national and sub-national levels. Outcome 5 (cross-cutting): The capacity of the Government and key stakeholders to assess progress in implementation of the Beijing Platform for Action and other global normative and policy frameworks is strengthened.

description.narrative:
UN Women Liberia has made substantive progress toward its Strategic Note (20202025) objectives, particularly in normative and coordination mandates. The 2024 Annual Report and CPE confirm strategic alignment with Liberias national priorities (PAPD, ARREST Agenda) and global frameworks (CEDAW, UNSCR 1325, Beijing 30).
Key results include: Normative work strengthened national gender policy frameworks, CEDAW reporting, and gender integration in the Armed Forces and land governance. WPS/WPP portfolios facilitated women's leadership in peacebuilding and local governance, with women holding 35% of ministerial roles and 31% deputy ministerial roles. Economic empowerment (WEE) demonstrated scalable innovations through the Buy from Women platform and digital literacy centers, benefiting over 3,000 women. EVAW programming supported FGM ban implementation through culturally sensitive approaches (Initiation without Mutilation) and community-led advocacy.
Outcome 1 Liberia has made substantial progress in advancing national development priorities, with a significant milestone being Lofa County becoming the fifth out of 11 counties officially declaring an end to FGM. UNW also supported drafting of the AntiFGM Bill, consolidating two previous drafts into one bill that is awaiting presentation to the House of Representatives. During the 80th Session of the UNGA, President Joseph Boakai announced a nationwide ban on FGM. This could be tied to UNW's work within the area.
Outcome 2 During the reporting period, 1137 jobs were created through initiatives supporting women's economic empowerment. The "Buy from Women" digital platform generated a total of USD 182 409 (LRD 35mil) of revenue, and was used by 1161 rural women farmers from 17 cooperatives in counties Lofa, Bong and Nimba. 207 new users registered on the platform in 2024. Since 2022, a total of 3619 women have benefited from training or equipment. UNW has equipped said women with clean energy tools for domestic and productive uses (solarpowered equipment such as Orange energy kits, mills, dryers, and ecostoves).
Outcome 3 Women in Liberia are increasingly taking on key leadership roles in resolving land dispute, ensuring their voices are central in decisionmaking on land ownership and use. This is done through structures like the Community Land Management and Development Committees where women and girls have an active role in shaping policies and resolutions that directly impact their communities. Through UNW's capacity strengthening, 52% of the local land dispute groups were trained to resolve conflicts and safeguard women's land rights. Furthermore, three new platforms where rural women actively decide on issues such as right to own and inherit land were set up. An important result of ongoing advocacy is the allocation of USD 250 000 by five government ministries and agencies, and one security and rule of law institution. These funds were specifically directed toward advancing gender equality within institutional structures and programming.
Outcome 4 Building on previously mentioned leadership and political achievements, womens representation in the ministerial cabinet rose to 35% (from 26.3 % in 2023), while deputy ministerial representation rose to 31% (from 23 % in 2023). Local governance also saw improvements, with women occupying 11% of appointments in local government, an increase from 8% in 2023. UNW contributed to integrating gender equality into the National Development Plan and the Country Development Agendas. This was done by working with the MFDP, MGCSP, and MIA to provide technical support to ensure gender mainstreaming throughout the plan. The Human Capital Development Pillar of the AAID reflects strengthened national commitment to gender equality and prioritizes investment in education, healthcare and the empowerment of women, youth, children, and persons with disabilities. Initial consultations for the National and County Development Plans recorded 24% female participation. The Women's Legislative Caucus of Liberia was supported in developing its 20242029 Strategic Plan.
Outcome 5 By providing substantive inputs, UNW supported the GoL in finalizing three major reports. The Beijing30 Periodic Progress report, the combined 9th and 10th CEDAW State Party report, and the report on the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and People's Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (Maputo Protocol) with the first report being officially submitted and the latter two awaiting formal government clearance. With contributions from Sweden, UNW facilitated the participation of four representatives (three female and one male) from the Liberian government and civil society at the 68th Commission on the Status of Women. A total of 31 participants (29 female, three male) represented Liberia at CSW68.
